- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, reduce forecasted price targets, especially in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >+5% from prior day), reduce the following 3–5 days’ forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is positive and price has recently been volatile or trending up, model tends to overreact — dampen the early forecast peak and favor gradual mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overestimates near-term upside — cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent 7-day average.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to reflect earlier correction than actual.  
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days of history show downward trend, model often underestimates the drop — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative signals (e.g., -1.00 repeated), model tends to ignore sentiment — force a 5–10% downward adjustment in forecast.
